description.narrative:
Over arching objective:
- Limit settlement activity in the West Bank, which violates Palestinian human rights, international law and which is intended to prevent the possibility for a two-state solution.
- Increase the likelihood of the emergence of a Palestinian state by limiting the development of the major obstacle to this process - the settlements.
Project outcomes are:
1. Through informing the Israeli public about settlement activities in the West Bank and East Jerusalem, and raising awareness of impact of settlement-related activities on democratic values the public develops a more accurate understanding of the ongoing problematics of the settlement project and its crucial role in perpetuating the occupation.
2. Through influencing Israeli office-holders to change their positions regarding settlement activity based on Peace Now's findings and analysis, legal precedents, verdicts, or policy changes can be utilized to challenge settlement activity.
3. Through influencing the international community, increase international pressure to halt settlement activity incentivises the Israeli government to change its calculus.

Kärnstöd för att mobilisera engagemang för fred baserat på en tvåstatslösning och skapandet av en Palestinsk stat sida vid sida med Israel, en lösning som skulle möjliggöra båda folkens rätt till självbestämmande. Bosättningarnas närvaro påverkar dessutom lokalbefolkningen negativt genom att bidra till brott mot mänskliga rättigheter på flera sätt. Genom programmet arbetar man med att kartlägga bosättningarnas expansion samt och motverka denna genom att informera allmänheten, lobba beslutsfattare och använda olika juridiska verktyg.

Peace Now is an Israeli movement that aims to mobilise the public for peace based on a two-state solution and the creation of a viable Palestinian state alongside Israel, allowing for both peoples' right to self-determination. The presence of settlements impacts local communities in several ways and maintains and exacerbates the oppression and human rights abuses of the Palestinian people. The program addresses settlement expansion as one of the key obstacles to a negotiated and viable peace

During the period, the cooperation partner has engaged awareness raising among the Israeli public, advocacy vis-a-vis Israeli office-holders as well as the international community, researching and monitoring settlement activities, engaging with the media, as well as legal work, all in order to limit further settlement expansions.
In terms of the cooperation partners legal work, several key achievements can be highlighted. In four High Court Justice Cases relating to constriction of outposts were brought by the cooperation partner In all for cases the High Court of Justice instructed the police to open investigations. These rulings are positive in the sense that they might deter authorities involved in illegal construction from continuing such activity, including the unlawful transfer of public funds towards the unlawful construction of outposts. However, the positive effects of these rulings are considerably reduced by the fact that the minister in charge of the Israeli police is a engaged in the settlement movement.
Another legal accomplishment was the petition launched by the cooperation partner demanding prior publication of land procedures, which the High Court agreed with. As a direct result of this, the Civil Administration has started to publish its intention to allocate thousands of dunams for grazing purposes. Owing to this publication, Palestinian residents were able to file objections to the planned allocation and thereby delaying its execution and potentially leading to its cancelation. Without the cooperation partners petitions, the allocation would have proceeded without any public notice, making it impossible to become aware of it or to challenge it.
Further, the cooperation partner contributed to international legal mechanisms by submitting a legal opinion to the International Court of Justice.
In terms of monitoring, it intensified during the period as a result of a sharp rise in settlement activity. The database expanded greatly, covering an additional 60 new settlements and outposts. In addition, 70 updates and 5 in-depth reports were published, compared to 59 updates and 4 in-depth reports in the previous year. Media coverage of the work of the cooperation partner in media also grew sharply, with over 700 media mentions as compared to 500 last year.
It is clear that the legal work of the cooperation partner has a very tangible impact on limiting or slowing the expansion of settlements. This is beneficial for the Palestinian communities concerned by the individual settlement our outpost, and also work towards promoting the conditions necessary to achieve a two-state solution in accordance with international law. Further, the cooperation partner remains a key resource when it comes to monitoring settlement expansions (and the involvement of the Israeli state) which is useful for the international community and for raising awareness among the Israeli public. It is however difficult to say with any certainty whether the monitoring of settlements and outposts has a tangible impact on Israeli public opinion.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
